properties.title: DINO Buildings
properties.description: Frozen DINOv3-ViT-S/16 (LVD1689M) encoder with a UperNet decoder, multi-task auxiliary heads (boundary + signed distance), and watershed instance separation, for binary building segmentation from very high resolution RGB aerial imagery. Decoder pretrained on hotosm/vhr-building-segmentation (~37k chips, OAM + OSM, global). Approximately 6.6x smaller than the dinov3l-buildings ViT-L variant (53M total params vs 343M, 462 MB ckpt vs 1.73 GB) for edge / constrained-infra deployment at a measurable accuracy cost. Intended for direct inference or decoder fine-tuning on small downstream OAM + OSM labelled sets (~100-200 chips).

fair:metrics_spec.name: Pixel IoU
fair:metrics_spec.description: Building-class pixel IoU on the val split: sum of intersection pixels divided by sum of union pixels across all val chips.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Instance Precision @ IoU>0.5
fair:metrics_spec.description: Fraction of predicted building instances that match a ground-truth instance at IoU>0.5 (panoptic-style matching via torchmetrics).

fair:metrics_spec.name: Instance Recall @ IoU>0.5
fair:metrics_spec.description: Fraction of ground-truth building instances matched by a prediction at IoU>0.5.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Instance F1 @ IoU>0.5
fair:metrics_spec.description: Harmonic mean of instance precision and recall, micro-averaged across the val split.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Predicted polygon avg vertices
fair:metrics_spec.description: Mean exterior vertex count across all predicted polygons after DP+MBR-safe regularisation, measured in each polygon's local UTM zone.

fair:metrics_spec.name: Predicted polygon orthogonality
fair:metrics_spec.description: Mean per-polygon fraction of edges within 5 degrees of the minimum-rotated-rectangle dominant axis. 1.0 = perfectly rectangular, near 0 = jagged/free-form.

fair:split_spec.description: Spatial block split on OAM-x-y-z tile coords: chips grouped into (x // block_size, y // block_size) blocks, whole blocks assigned to train or val. Non-OAM filenames fall back to a seeded random split.

fair:hyperparameters_spec.description: Decoder fine-tuning epochs
Training batch size
AdamW learning rate (decoder only; encoder is frozen)
AdamW weight decay
Fraction of chips held out as spatial val. Blocks are added to val until this share of total chips is reached.
Seed for block ordering in the spatial split
Side length (in TMS tile units) of the spatial block that holds adjacent chips together; larger blocks = stronger spatial separation, fewer blocks to split.
Within-train holdout that upstream finetune uses for Lightning's per-epoch val_loss/val_iou and early stopping. Independent of the catalog-facing spatial val.
Keep the DINOv3 encoder frozen (recommended)

Input normalisation source. 'hot_global' uses mean/std from the hotosm/vhr-building-segmentation dataset (matches pretraining). 'dataset' computes per-channel mean/std from the user's finetune chips, pick this when your imagery differs substantially from HOT global imagery.
Sigmoid threshold for building mask
Douglas-Peucker tolerance in metres (EPSG:3857). 0 disables simplification.
Minimum polygon-area / MBR-area ratio for the rectangle-substitution step. Lower = more aggressive squaring of corners.
Maximum new neighbour overlap (m^2) allowed when substituting a polygon with its MBR. Keeps adjacent buildings from being merged.
Drop polygons smaller than this area (m^2). Filters specks from sub-pixel artefacts.

Minimum pixel distance between watershed seeds picked from the predicted distance map. Larger values merge adjacent instances into a single building; smaller values split touching buildings more aggressively.

Connected-component area (pixels) above which a foreground blob is treated as large and split using distance-map h-maxima seeds instead of peak-local-max. Lower splits smaller merged clumps; higher leaves more touching buildings merged.

Prominence (normalised distance units) of the h-maxima used to seed watershed splits inside large blobs. Higher gives fewer, more confident splits (less over-segmentation); lower splits more aggressively.

Pixel step between 256x256 sliding windows at inference. Smaller strides overlap more (slower, marginally smoother stitching); larger strides cut window count and latency. 192 is ~1.9x faster than 128 at near-identical F1; 256 is tiling with no overlap.

Optuna trials run after training to find inference post-processing params that maximise F1 + 0.3 * mean_iou on the val set. Set to 0 to skip and use the catalog defaults. Requires at least 8 val chips; smaller val sets fall back to defaults with a warning.
Fraction of the train split actually loaded by the upstream dataloader (maps to dinov3_hot cfg.data_pct). Set to a small value in CI smoke runs to keep memory and time low. 1.0 uses everything.
